newsitem.title: USA: USDA develops new more accurate test for E. Coli.
newsitem.headline: USDA develops new more accurate test for E. Coli.

text.p: A new, more accurate test for potentially deadly strains of the E. Coli bacteria should boost food safety and greatly reduce industry testing costs, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday.

"When you get a positive result, you can be very confident you have a problem," said Dr. William Laegreid, leader of the USDA animal health research team in Clay Center, Nebraska that developed the test with Meridian Diagnostics Inc. of Cincinnati. Current tests are not so accurate, he said.
Meridian will soon begin marketing the tests for close to $10 each, Laegreid said.
"Many other tests give a significant number of false positives," which is very costly for industry and discourages voluntary testing, Laegreid said. "This is a very accurate test," he said.

In 1993, E. Coli O157:H7 was responsible for the deaths of children in the Pacific Northwest. Just this week, Hudson Foods Inc voluntarily recalled 40,000 pounds of frozen hamburgers because of possible E. Coli contamination.
Like other rapid tests now available, the new test still requires overnight incubation, Laegreid said.
However, standard culture methods require a 48-hour incubation period, "which is a huge amount of time" for hamburger processors to keep their product in storage awaiting results, Laegreid said.
In a separate news release, Meridian said its new ImmunoCard STAT! O157:H7 test "utilizes two highly-specific monoclonal antibodies" to detect the E. Coli bacteria within minutes.
The Center for Disease Control and Prevention estimates that 20,000 cases of E. Coli O157:H7 may occur each year, resulting in hundreds of deaths.
